no humans, arrows, wooden target, close-up, three-quarter view, dutch angle, solid background, hand-drawn linework, painterly

A thick battered wooden archery target fills the right half and extends outside the right frame, its front plane angled toward the left. Exactly THREE arrows point diagonally from lower-left toward upper-right into three closely spaced points on this same target. Two arrows are already embedded, their small dark shafts and two plain feather fins extending back toward the left. The third arrow is arriving just below them: its steel tip touches the wood with one tiny pale notch and two short splinters. One short muted ivory motion streak behind the arriving arrow implies the next shot, not a simultaneous fan volley. Background is one uniform solid deep petrol-blue color, no landscape.

Firm economical colored contour lines close the three arrow silhouettes and target rim; sparse structural lines show penetration points and thickness. Broad matte gray-brown and umber planes describe wood, slate-gray shafts and quiet ochre feather shapes. Inside contours, a few opaque long brush swipes turn material; no finely painted grain or ornate target pattern. Keep a small strongest highlight at the arriving arrow contact. Large calm shapes and distinct three-shot rhythm dominate.

masterpiece, best quality, painterly, sketch, visible brush strokes, loose hand-painted texture, broken edges, blocky volume modeling.

A complete illustration with the freshness of a painted sketch, not an unfinished draft. Soft directional light reveals the planes of forms. Build volumes from confident planes of light and shadow with visible brush edges, while letting selected outer contours remain open. Use broad flowing paint masses, dry uneven strokes, and crisp small highlights appropriate to each material. Vary the brush size and edge sharpness between different materials. Preserve deliberate brush marks instead of smoothing every surface.
